newsitem.title: UK: European trade worried about NY coffee delivery.
newsitem.headline: European trade worried about NY coffee delivery.

text.p: The European Coffee Federation (ECF) has voiced concerns over what it called the "inadequacy" of the New York arabica coffee futures market, especially with regard to the availability of deliverable coffee.
The matter was raised at the group's annual meeting in Vienna earlier this week. The ECF groups the region's roasters and traders.
ECF secretary-general Roland Vaessen said on Thursday the members were concerned about whether there was sufficient deliverable coffee for all the traded contracts on the market.
"Can the terminal market under present circumtances perform adequately?" he asked. "Is there any coffee available for delivery if you let your contract mature?"
Vaessen said although actual physical deliveries in a futures market was very seldom, "delivery is possible and should be possible."
"It is entirely within the rules of the terminal market," he added.
New York's arabica futures have rallied sharply since early this year on the back of low stocks and tight supply from Latin America.
Lower certified stocks on the New York exchange was one of the factors for the rally, which saw prices hitting a 20-year-peak of $3.18 per lb last week.

The Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC), in a separate statement, said it was ready to discuss with the industry, trade and the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange on possible measures to overcome the problems of the coffee contract.
It said the U.S. market should be allowed to work effectively as a truly price discovery mechanism for all sectors involved in the coffee trade.
